note: Brain-penetrant tubulin agents (sagopilone, patupilone, verubulin, lexibulin, lisavanbulin) entered recurrent-GBM trials on rodent brain-PK and orthotopic-xenograft data; tumour exposure held in patients, efficacy did not.
label: Glioblastoma (tubulin)

engagement.note: Tubulin engagement inferred from intracranial tumour shrinkage in mice; no patient-tumour mitotic-arrest or tubulin readout found in any GBM trial.
engagement.quote: Sagopilone exhibited significant antitumor activity in both the U373 and U87 models of human glioblastoma, while paclitaxel showed a limited effect in the U373 model.
engagement.judgement: Model-side engagement markers exist (G2/M arrest in vitro; phospho-histone H3 rise in orthotopic GBM PDX, Burgenske 2022, doi:10.1093/neuonc/noab162) but no GBM trial of any agent in the class reported a tubulin-engagement or mitotic-arrest readout in patient tumour. Oehler 2012 analysed drug-exposed resected tissue only for response-predictive biomarkers (Ki-67 etc.), not engagement, so it is placed under dose.

dose.model: Rodent brain/tumour pharmacokinetics (rats bearing glioma, nude mice)
dose.note: Patupilone was retained in rodent tumour and brain with no apparent elimination over 24 h; the class's BBB-penetration claim rests on such data.
dose.quote: but showed longer retention in tumor and brain with no apparent elimination over 24 h.
dose.judgement: Earliest verified rodent brain-PK paper for an agent that then went into a GBM trial; the same model type (rat/mouse autoradiography and brain:plasma ratios) underpinned sagopilone (Hoffmann 2009), verubulin (Sirisoma 2009, doi:10.1021/jm801315b) and lisavanbulin (Burgenske 2022). Quote is a verbatim clause of the abstract's results sentence.

dose.model: Rodent brain/tumour pharmacokinetics (rats bearing glioma, nude mice)
dose.note: Patupilone given a week before re-resection reached 30× plasma concentration in recurrent GBM tissue, as rodent brain retention had predicted.
dose.quote: At the time of surgery, the concentration of patupilone in tumor tissue was 30 times higher than in the plasma.
dose.judgement: Abstract only (Karger paywall). The paper itself states the rodent BBB-crossing premise and reports the patient tissue:plasma ratio, so comparison_stated is true, but it gives no rodent ratio to compare against, hence direction_only and source_calls_it null. Caveat: tissue came from contrast-enhancing recurrent GBM at re-resection, where the BBB is disrupted, so this tests tumour exposure, not intact-BBB penetration. No other agent in the class measured brain or tumour drug levels in patients (sagopilone, verubulin, lisavanbulin trials report plasma PK only), so the status rests on nine patients and one drug. Registry NCT00715013 has no posted results.

efficacy.note: Sagopilone almost completely prevented growth of intracerebral U373 and U87 tumours; this and rodent brain penetration were the basis for GBM trials.
efficacy.quote: Sagopilone demonstrated significant antitumor activity in orthotopic models of both glioblastoma and CNS metastases compared with paclitaxel or temozolomide, underlining the value of further research evaluating sagopilone in the treatment of brain tumors.
efficacy.judgement: Opens the strip at the earliest orthotopic-GBM efficacy model verified within budget. Earlier taxane/vinca-era intracranial models (1990s) were not searched; if found they would move model_first_use_year earlier without changing any status.

efficacy.note: EORTC phase II: no objective responses, PFS6 6.7%, despite near-complete growth inhibition in the orthotopic model; authors call it a miss.
efficacy.quote: Despite encouraging preclinical data, including almost complete growth inhibition in an orthotopic glioma model, […] we could not detect any evidence of relevant clinical antitumor activity in recurrent glioblastoma.
efficacy.judgement: Full text read (PMC3164435). The quoted discussion sentence is 51 words in the source; the bracketed ellipsis elides only its pharmacokinetic/toxicity clause. Same-direction evidence not given separate entries: verubulin (brain:plasma claim from mice, Sirisoma 2009) had limited activity in 56 recurrent-GBM patients and accrual stopped for futility (Chamberlain 2014, doi:10.1007/s11060-014-1437-y; phase I Grossmann 2012, doi:10.1007/s11060-012-0964-7), but neither paper makes a model comparison. Lexibulin/CYT997's GBM study NCT00650949 was terminated with no posted results and no publication. A 15-patient mixed-glioma trial (Silvani 2009, doi:10.1007/s11060-009-9890-8, PFS-6 33%) claimed activity but did not state a model comparison and Stupp calls those patients possibly very selected, so it is not scored as a prior 'same'. Registry NCT00424060 has no posted results.

efficacy.model: Orthotopic GBM6 stem-like xenografts with EB1 as response biomarker (later a 14-line GBM PDX panel)
efficacy.note: New patient-derived orthotopic model: EB1-high tumours gained survival from lisavanbulin, proposing EB1 to select responders.
efficacy.quote: These results support the potential of BAL101553 for glioblastoma treatment, with EB1 expression as a predictive biomarker of response.
efficacy.judgement: Abstract only (MCT paywall). Status reset to untested because the class moved to a different, better model: patient-derived orthotopic stem-like xenografts with a biomarker, later a 14-line intracranial GBM PDX panel (Burgenske 2022, doi:10.1093/neuonc/noab162; benefit in 9/14 lines, brain:plasma 1.3–1.6). The lisavanbulin program relied on this model: the sponsor built a CLIA EB1 assay and enrolled only EB1-positive patients in phase 2a (NCT02490800).

efficacy.model: Orthotopic GBM6 stem-like xenografts with EB1 as response biomarker (later a 14-line GBM PDX panel)
efficacy.note: Prospective EB1-positive cohort did not enrich for response (1 PR/9); phase 2a closed; authors say the model's biomarker was not confirmed.
efficacy.quote: Our experience in this study did not confirm EB1 as a reliable predictor of response to lisavanbulin.
efficacy.judgement: Full text read (PMC12208313). The paper's introduction restates the orthotopic-model prediction and its discussion rejects it, so comparison_stated is true; a 5-gene RNA signature replaced EB1 post hoc. Durable responses did occur (3 of 37 relapsed brain-tumour patients, two IDH-mutant), so the model was wrong about who responds rather than about any activity. The IV phase 2a (Joerger 2023, doi:10.1007/s10637-023-01336-9; NCT02895360, results posted 2021-10-11) reported 1 PR/12 unselected GBM patients without a model comparison and is not scored. registry_date is the results-first-posted date of NCT02490800.
